request.prompt: The same Hush Garden seen straight down from high above, a true top-down plan with no perspective tilt, the maze square and centred. The hedge-topped walls draw the lanes as a clear maze pattern with loops; the four quarters' floor colours divide it; the round watchtower roof is the dot in the centre court; the small sundial court in the north-west quarter, the dark sculk-ringed well in the south-west corner, four bells at the quarters' middles, and the gate tower on the middle of the east edge opening onto the meadow.
request.style_note: The Hush Garden, in one hand throughout: a Minecraft world of whole cubic blocks, drawn as a clean, bright, in-game view with the blocky voxel look of the game (no smooth shapes, no realistic foliage), warm late-afternoon sun low in the west, long soft shadows, a light pastel palette, cheerful and inviting, a small co-op game's level. Maze walls are mossy stone brick four blocks high capped with clipped oak-leaf hedge; lane floors are paved in soft colours by quarter: rose-pink terracotta in the north-west, butter-yellow in the north-east, pale sky-blue in the south-east, mint-green in the south-west. Each image is ONE single full-frame view of that place, filling the frame edge to edge: never a sheet, never a grid, never a panel, never an inset, never a caption, label, border or text.
